method: Fresh mpmath dps=120 recomputation of the Log-LFR survival Gbar(x)=ln(1-(1-p)exp(-a x-b x^2/2))/ln p and series survival prod_i Gbar_i; common p (per printed eqs 29-30). No eval-script code reused.

claims.independent_witness: Eval instance alpha=(1/2,3,5), beta=(1/4,1/2,3) vs alpha*=(1,4,6), beta*=(1/2,1,4), p=1/3 — componentwise alpha<=alpha*, beta<=beta* verified. Fbar_{X1:3}-Fbar_{Y1:3} = +4.55e-12 at x=1e-12 (eval's witness confirmed), +0.0794993 at x=0.1, +0.0024366 at x=0.5, +8.48e-6 at x=1 — positive at every tested abscissa, so X_{1:3} >=st Y_{1:3} holds and the printed X_{1:3} <=st Y_{1:3} fails.
claims.evidence: The Log-LFR component survival is decreasing in alpha and beta (a quick monotonicity check on d Gbar/d alpha <0), so larger alpha*,beta* shrink Y's survival — the true conclusion is the REVERSED order X_{1:n} >=st Y_{1:n}. The paper's own proof in fact derives F_{X1:n}(x) <= F_{Y1:n}(x) (printed eq. 31: '1-prod_X <= 1-prod_Y' follows from the correctly-derived eq. 32 alpha_i x+ beta_i x^2/2 <= alpha*_i x + beta*_i x^2/2), which IS X_{1:n} >=st Y_{1:n}; the preamble 'we need to prove Fbar_X <= Fbar_Y' and the printed conclusion contain a direction slip, not just a numerical accident. Genuine direction-reversed refutation.
